proof.verificationCase: binds every executable release surface to the package version

claims.blockedReason: The claim is what every consumer's first command reports, so it needs CONSENTED remote evidence: a published `mjolnir-qa@<version>` install observed from outside this checkout. No such observation exists and none can be manufactured from inside the tree that produced the tarball — that is what `scripts/revalidate-claims.mjs` §THE RULE calls self-derivation. The local half is verified continuously by the named verificationCase.

proof.verificationCase: re-derives every assignment from the hash

claims.expiry: on rule or detector revision change
claims.blockedReason: The census is generated FROM the verdict corpus, so the corpus cannot be the evidence that the census is right — every verdict it summarises is its own input. `docs/HOLDOUT-SPLIT.json` now exists and is the artifact this blocker asked for: a deterministic partition of the corpus repositories into measurement and holdout, gated by `npm run holdout:split`, with the exclusion derived from `isCoreCandidate` rather than declared. TWO things are still missing and both are why `proof` stays empty. (1) No holdout EVALUATION has been run against it — the split labels the repositories, it does not yet report a held-out false-positive rate, and a labelled partition nobody scored is not evidence. (2) The split is still produced by this repository, so it answers 'was the partition chosen honestly' and not 'was the classifier scored by someone else'. Promoting this needs either an externally-run evaluation or an owner ruling that a repo-level deterministic split satisfies the independence requirement. The measured count remains drift-locked by `tests/contract/census-drift.spec.ts` in the meantime.

proof.verificationCase: output carries the shipped structural markers

claims.blockedReason: The marker is a string both the reporter and the workflow emit, and both sides are in this tree. A consumer-side observation — a PR comment fetched back from the GitHub API on a repository that is not this one — is the only evidence that is not the claim restating itself. That needs a token and an external repository, neither of which belongs in a PR gate.

An internal approval recorded in the same repository that produced the model is the shape of self-certification this registry exists to refuse, so the claim stays BLOCKED until an external reviewer is named. `docs/adr/0012-hosted-enterprise-boundary.md` records the boundary decision.
